contexts.text: However plainly they may be demonstrated.
If it were demonstrated they would not believe.
As has been demonstrated above. DLW 209:2. DLW 225:end. DLW 230. DLW 231. DLW 242. DLW 242. DLW 282. DLW 304. DLW 359. DP 54. DP 210. TCR 37:2.
It is not allowable to demonstrate this matter, except by means of universals.
Here, it is to be demonstrated. DLW 260.
This will be fully demonstrated in what follows. DP 218, etc. TCR 329:2. TCR 336. TCR 395. TCR 395:end. TCR 603.
Time fails to demonstrate these things more at large.
To demonstrate or confirm anything by means of things unknown places a subject in obscurity.
These things are to be demonstrated by like things elsewhere in the Word. AR 285.
That envy and pain thence arising... might be effectively demonstrated.
That each and all things may, in Heaven, be demonstrated to the light.
This can demonstrate nothing, except that such a man cannot enter the other life...

Faith without sight... spurns and rejects all demonstration; just as one who sees an object refuses to have it demonstrated to him that he sees it... For an object that is demonstrated to be seen which is already seen is called into doubt, for such demonstration is attended with this. Therefore demonstrations are only for those who want to believe nothing unless they see it. Lest such should remain in their blindness, and be further blinded, things are to be demonstrated which ought not to be demonstrated; as, for example, that there is a God, which everyone ought to believe without demonstrating arguments; whereas it is usually the case that when this is demonstrated, in every argument there is contained something of doubt.
Nor can this phantasy be taken away from them, except by means of living demonstrations.
A thousand proofs of experience have demonstrated this to me to the very sense.
